record.original_question: For ground, variable-free term-rewriting systems, what is the complexity of deciding confluence?

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of the decision problem for the confluence of ground term-rewriting systems?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A ground term-rewriting system over a finite signature Σ is a finite set R of rewrite rules ℓ → r where ℓ and r are variable-free (ground) terms in T(Σ). The one-step rewrite relation →_R on T(Σ) is defined by s →_R t iff t is obtained from s by replacing some subterm occurrence equal to ℓ by r for some rule ℓ → r ∈ R. Let →*_R denote its reflexive-transitive closure. The system R is confluent if for all terms s, t₁, t₂ ∈ T(Σ) with s →*_R t₁ and s →*_R t₂, there exists u ∈ T(Σ) such that t₁ →*_R u and t₂ →*_R u.

Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem: given as input a finite signature Σ and a finite ground term-rewriting system R over Σ, decide whether R is confluent. In particular, provide tight upper and lower complexity bounds.
artifact.status_search_result: Confluence of ground term-rewriting systems was shown decidable in polynomial time by Comon, Godoy, and Nieuwenhuis (2001), and subsequent work by Felgenhauer (2012) gave a cubic-time algorithm. Thus the question of polynomial-time decidability is resolved, with current best upper bound O(n³).

status_evidence.title: The confluence of ground term rewrite systems is decidable in polynomial time
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time decidability of confluence for ground term rewrite systems.

status_evidence.snippet: Cubic-time algorithm for deciding confluence of ground term rewrite systems.
